s: MaxLinear DEF 14A filed 2 Apr 2026: Seendripu beneficially owned 5,434,243 shares as of 23 Mar 2026, 6.0 percent; MXL closed 66.61 dollars on 21 Aug 2026 (stockanalysis.com)
m: Beneficial ownership times market close: 5,434,243 x 66.61 = 362 million dollars. Includes 370,061 common, 296,084 options, 66,200 RSUs and 604,899 deferred vested units per proxy footnote 1.
did: Co-founded MaxLinear in September 2003 in Carlsbad to build television and broadband tuners in plain CMOS instead of the discrete can tuners then standard, took it public in 2010, and bought Entropic in 2015, Exar in 2017 and Intel's home gateway chip line in 2020.
why: Nobody believed a sensitive RF tuner could work in a standard digital CMOS process. Doing it there meant the tuner and demodulator collapsed onto one die and the price fell with every node shrink, while incumbents were stuck selling multi-chip modules built on specialty processes.
obst: The 3.8 billion dollar Silicon Motion acquisition collapsed in July 2023 when Chinese regulatory clearance never arrived and MaxLinear walked, drawing an arbitration claim; revenue then fell from 1.12 billion in 2022 to 361 million in 2024 as broadband customers unwound inventory.
turn: The 2020 purchase of Intel's Home Gateway Platform Division for about 150 million dollars, which turned a tuner-chip supplier into a full broadband gateway system-on-chip vendor.

s: Treasury Wine Estates announcement 31 Oct 2023: acquisition of DAOU Vineyards for US 900 million upfront plus up to 100 million earn-out; age from DAOU Systems DEF 14A filed 21 Apr 1998, which lists Georges J. Daou at 36
m: Announced 900 million dollar upfront price for a business the founding brothers owned, split evenly, less an assumed 30 percent long-term capital gains and vineyard debt: 900 / 2 x 0.7 is about 315 million; held to 250 million as a conservative floor.
did: Fled Lebanon's civil war as a teenager, co-founded healthcare IT firm DAOU Systems in San Diego in 1987 and took it public on Nasdaq in 1997, then bought the 212-acre former Hoffman Mountain Ranch above Paso Robles in 2007 and built DAOU Vineyards, sold to Treasury Wine Estates in 2023.
why: Paso Robles Cabernet land cost roughly a tenth of Napa's. Selling 90-point Cabernet at 20 to 40 dollars through national chain distribution built a 400,000-case luxury brand on cheap dirt, and Treasury needed exactly that price tier to fill the gap between Beringer and Penfolds.
obst: A shell hit the family home in Beirut and the family fled to France with nothing; two decades later DAOU Systems collapsed after 1998 revenue restatements and shareholder suits, and the brothers left the company they had founded.
turn: The 2007 purchase of the derelict Hoffman Mountain Ranch, the 2,200-foot calcareous limestone site the brothers renamed DAOU Mountain.

s: Treasury Wine Estates announcement 31 Oct 2023: acquisition of DAOU Vineyards for US 900 million upfront plus up to 100 million earn-out; age from DAOU Systems DEF 14A filed 21 Apr 1998, which lists Daniel J. Daou at 32
m: Announced 900 million dollar upfront price for a business the founding brothers owned, split evenly, less an assumed 30 percent long-term capital gains and vineyard debt: 900 / 2 x 0.7 is about 315 million; held to 250 million as a conservative floor.
did: Co-founded DAOU Systems in San Diego with his brother in 1987 and served as its president, then became winemaker of DAOU Vineyards from its 2007 founding, personally making the Cabernets that carried the brand to about 400,000 cases before the 2023 Treasury Wine Estates sale.
why: He treated Paso Robles as a soil problem rather than a marketing one, planting to the calcareous clay of the west side and blending for a Napa flavour profile at a Paso cost base, which is why a region priced as bulk fruit produced a luxury brand in fifteen years.
obst: He nearly died in the Lebanese civil war shelling that drove the family out of Beirut; the brothers then lost their first company when DAOU Systems restated results in 1998 and the shares fell from the mid-thirties to under two dollars.
turn: Deciding in 2007 to buy an abandoned mountain vineyard rather than a working winery, and replanting it entirely to Bordeaux varieties.

s: Halozyme DEF 14A filed 23 Mar 2026: Torley beneficially owned 2,208,873 shares as of 9 Mar 2026, 1.8 percent, including 1,441,093 exercisable options; HALO closed 108.17 dollars on 21 Aug 2026 (stockanalysis.com)
m: Beneficial ownership times market close: 2,208,873 x 108.17 = 239 million dollars, gross of the exercise price on the option component and of tax.
did: Became Halozyme CEO in January 2014 and turned a failing oncology drug developer into a royalty business licensing its ENHANZE hyaluronidase to Roche, Janssen, Takeda and argenx so their intravenous biologics could be injected under the skin; revenue went from 55 million in 2013 to 1.40 billion in 2025.
why: Subcutaneous conversion extends a biologic's franchise past its intravenous patent cliff, so the licensee pays a royalty to protect billions in revenue. Owning the only proven recombinant human hyaluronidase meant Halozyme captured that toll without running a single commercial sales force.
obst: The HALO-301 pancreatic cancer Phase 3 failed in January 2019 and wiped out the proprietary pipeline; she cut more than half the workforce, abandoned oncology development and rebuilt the company as a licensor, then had to defend the enzyme patents against Merck's Alteogen-based subcutaneous Keytruda.
turn: The January 2019 PEGPH20 failure and the decision weeks later to stop developing drugs at all and become a platform licensor.

s: AppFolio DEF 14A filed 28 Apr 2025: Bliss beneficially owned 903,290 Class B shares, 7.0 percent, address P.O. Box 50440 Santa Barbara CA 93150, age 72; Form 4 filed 9 Jun 2025 adds 10,405 Class A; APPF closed 224.40 dollars on 21 Aug 2026
m: 913,695 combined Class A and Class B shares x 224.40 = 205 million dollars. Treated as a floor: his other holdings through Investment Group of Santa Barbara are not disclosed.
did: As a partner of Investment Group of Santa Barbara he backed and helped found AppFolio in 2006, sat on its board from 2008, and held roughly 7 percent of the property-management software company through its 2015 IPO and its run to an 8 billion dollar market value.
why: IGSB's model was to fund a small number of Santa Barbara software companies at inception and never sell, so the compounding stayed with the founders rather than the funds. Holding dual-class B stock through two decades of AppFolio's growth is why one seed position is now worth more than 200 million.
obst: AppFolio sold into small property managers who had never bought software, a segment RealPage and Yardi had written off as too fragmented to serve; it took nine years of subscale revenue before the 2015 IPO validated the market.
turn: AppFolio's June 2015 Nasdaq listing, which converted a nine-year private position into public stock he did not sell.

s: Prometheus Biosciences DEFM14A filed 16 May 2023: at Merck's 200.00 dollar per share price McKenna's equity was 206,647,761 in vested option spread, 184,629,465 unvested and 7,422,600 in RSUs, total 398,699,826, plus 26,039,295 in tax reimbursement; age 42 in the DEF 14A of 28 Apr 2022
m: 398.7 million dollars of option and RSU value is ordinary income; net of combined California and federal rates of about 50 percent that is roughly 200 million, plus the disclosed 26 million tax gross-up and retained founder equity in Mirador Therapeutics.
did: Took over Prometheus in 2019 when it was a Cedars-Sinai spinout sitting on an inflammatory bowel disease biobank, listed it at 19 dollars in March 2021, read out the anti-TL1A antibody PRA023 in December 2022 and sold the company to Merck for 10.8 billion dollars at 200 dollars a share in 2023.
why: The Cedars-Sinai patient database let Prometheus pick TL1A and pre-select genetic responders with a companion diagnostic before dosing anyone, so a Phase 2 in ulcerative colitis produced an effect size nobody else in inflammatory bowel disease could show and forced an auction.
obst: TL1A had been passed over by every large pharma as an unproven target; Prometheus priced its IPO at 19 dollars and traded near 12 through mid-2022 with a single Phase 2 asset and no partner.
turn: 7 December 2022, the ARTEMIS-UC Phase 2 result, which tripled the stock overnight and started the process that ended with Merck.

s: Inhibrx Biosciences DEF 14A filed 26 Apr 2026: Lappe beneficially owned 1,075,413 shares, 7.29 percent, age 59; Inhibrx DEFM14A filed 26 Apr 2024 shows 3,194,717 Inhibrx shares at Sanofi's 30.00 dollar cash price; INBX closed 103.63 dollars on 21 Aug 2026
m: Live stake 1,075,413 x 103.63 = 111 million dollars, of which 925,413 are outright shares. Plus roughly 96 million gross of Sanofi cash in 2024, taken at about 60 million after tax on the option portion. Total held to 170 million.
did: Co-founded Inhibrx in La Jolla in 2010 to build multivalent single-domain antibodies, sold the alpha-1 antitrypsin program INBRX-101 to Sanofi for about 2.2 billion dollars in January 2024, and spun the remaining pipeline out as Inhibrx Biosciences, where he is chief executive.
why: The single-domain format let him hang three or four binding heads off one molecule and tune valency precisely. Death-receptor agonism had failed for twenty years because bivalent antibodies cluster the receptor too weakly; tetravalent binding is what made INBRX-109 work in chondrosarcoma.
obst: Inhibrx spent a decade on venture and crossover money with no approved product, in a target class littered with failures from Amgen, Genentech and Daiichi Sankyo; the 2020 IPO came before any pivotal data existed.
turn: 23 January 2024, when Sanofi agreed to buy the company for one asset and hand the rest of the pipeline back to shareholders as a separate listed company.

s: Viking Therapeutics DEF 14A filed 22 Apr 2026: Lian beneficially owned 4,139,349 shares as of 15 Mar 2026, 3.5 percent, comprising 2,430,220 shares and 1,709,129 exercisable options, age 60; VKTX closed 33.89 dollars on 21 Aug 2026
m: Outright shares 2,430,220 x 33.89 = 82 million dollars, plus in-the-money spread on 1,709,129 exercisable options at a weighted strike near 9 dollars, about 43 million. Total roughly 125 million.
did: Founded Viking Therapeutics in September 2012 as a sell-side analyst with no lab, in-licensed a shelved metabolic portfolio from Ligand Pharmaceuticals, and developed VK2735, the dual GLP-1 and GIP agonist that produced 14.7 percent mean weight loss at 13 weeks in the 2024 VENTURE trial.
why: He bought compounds another company had already spent the discovery money on and written off, so a firm of a few dozen people only had to fund clinical work. That is the only way a company that size could put a competitive obesity asset next to Lilly and Novo Nordisk.
obst: Viking listed at 8 dollars in 2015 and traded under 2 dollars through 2016 and 2017 with going-concern-level cash, while Ligand's retained stake and warrants overhung the equity; he had been an equity analyst, never a drug developer.
turn: 27 February 2024, the VK2735 Phase 2 obesity readout, after which the stock rose 121 percent in a single session.

s: RayzeBio SC 14D-9 filed 25 Jan 2024: Song held 1,622,095 shares worth 101,380,938 dollars and 1,353,370 in-the-money options with 70,029,751 of spread at Bristol Myers Squibb's 62.50 dollar tender price; age 48 in the 424B4 of 15 Sep 2023
m: 171.4 million dollars gross at the tender price. Net of long-term capital gains on founder shares and ordinary rates on 392,073 restricted shares and the option spread, about 100 million, plus retained founder equity in Candid Therapeutics.
did: Co-founded RayzeBio in San Diego in 2020 to build actinium-225 targeted radiopharmaceuticals, listed it at 18 dollars in September 2023 in the worst biotech IPO window in fifteen years, and sold it to Bristol Myers Squibb for 4.1 billion dollars three months later.
why: The binding constraint in alpha-emitter therapy was not biology but isotope: world actinium-225 supply ran to a few curies a year. Contracting that supply and building his own Indianapolis radiopharmacy first made RayzeBio the only buyable asset once Novartis proved the market with Pluvicto.
obst: He had to commit to isotope supply and a manufacturing plant before RB-1 had any pivotal data, and then price an IPO into a market where biotech listings were being pulled; the stock broke issue within weeks.
turn: 26 December 2023, when Bristol Myers Squibb agreed to pay 62.50 dollars a share in cash, 247 percent above the IPO price set three months earlier.

s: SOLV Energy 424B4 filed 29 May 2026: Hershman holds 4,023,320 Class B shares after the offering, 5.0 percent, age 56; IPO price 25.00 dollars, MWH closed 28.34 dollars on 21 Aug 2026 (stockanalysis.com)
m: Paired Class B shares and Holdings LLC units are exchangeable one for one into Class A: 4,023,320 x 28.34 = 114 million dollars.
did: Ran Swinerton Renewable Energy from 2017, led its December 2021 carve-out from the parent builder into a standalone company backed by American Securities, renamed it SOLV Energy, and grew it into the largest utility-scale solar construction contractor in the United States before its 2026 NYSE listing.
why: Utility-scale solar engineering and construction is a bonding and manpower business: a developer needs a contractor who can put a thousand people on a site and absorb schedule risk. Owning the crews before the 2022 tax-credit extension locked in a decade of volume meant the work had nowhere else to go.
obst: The 2022 Auxin Solar anti-circumvention petition froze module imports and stalled projects already under construction, and the 2023 rate shock pushed developers to defer builds, all within two years of taking the company independent with leverage on it.
turn: December 2021, buying the renewables division out of Swinerton with American Securities rather than staying a unit inside a general contractor.

s: Neurocrine Biosciences DEF 14A filed 30 Apr 2026: Gano beneficially owned 635,601 shares as of 31 Mar 2026, age 53, and realised 7,053,200 dollars on option exercises plus 1,314,170 on vesting in 2025 alone; NBIX closed 152.57 dollars on 21 Aug 2026
m: 635,601 x 152.57 = 97 million dollars of current beneficial ownership, plus 8.4 million pre-tax realised in 2025 and further sales across nineteen years at the company; held to 110 million.
did: Joined Neurocrine in 2007 just after the indiplon rejection nearly killed it, ran business development for fifteen years including the 2020 Takeda deal that brought in seven pipeline programmes, and became chief executive in January 2024, launching Crenessity for congenital adrenal hyperplasia that December.
why: Neurocrine's model was to buy de-risked central nervous system assets rather than discover them, and Gano ran that side. Ingrezza's 2017 approval gave the company a cash engine that let it keep in-licensing while rivals had to raise dilutive equity for every programme.
obst: He arrived at a company the FDA had just rejected, whose stock had fallen roughly 80 percent and which had cut most of its staff; there was no approved product for the first decade of his tenure.
turn: April 2017, when Ingrezza became the first drug approved for tardive dyskinesia and took Neurocrine from no revenue to more than 2 billion dollars a year.
